claims.text: Urine pregnancy test in every female of childbearing age.
claims.quote: All females of childbearing age should be given a urine pregnancy test.

claims.text: Severe vomiting, vomiting over 1 day, or dehydration: electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, glucose, urinalysis, sometimes liver tests.
claims.quote: Patients with severe vomiting, vomiting lasting over 1 day, or signs of dehydration on examination should have other laboratory tests (eg, electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, glucose, urinalysis, sometimes liver tests).

claims.text: Red flag findings: test for the cause the symptoms suggest.
claims.quote: Patients with red flag findings should have testing appropriate to the symptoms

claims.text: Acute vomiting with diarrhea in a healthy patient with a benign exam is very likely infectious gastroenteritis; further assessment can wait.
claims.quote: Acute vomiting accompanied by diarrhea in an otherwise healthy patient with a benign examination is highly likely to be infectious gastroenteritis; further assessment may be deferred.

claims.text: Chronic vomiting: the same labs plus upper endoscopy, small-bowel radiographs, and gastric emptying and motility tests.
claims.quote: The assessment of chronic vomiting usually includes the previously listed laboratory tests plus upper GI endoscopy, small-bowel radiographs, and tests to assess gastric emptying and antral-duodenal motility.
